zh: 对于成功地使用 AI 工具、Lovable，以及更广泛地使用，你开发了哪些专业技巧？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are maybe two or three things you've learned that help you be really good at this job?
zh: 也许有两三件事是你学到的，帮助你在这份工作中表现出色？

speaker: Unknown
en: The first understanding that I had very early on, even though just in full transparency before we begin, I don't have a technical background.
zh: 我很早就有的第一个理解是，尽管在我们开始之前完全透明地说，我没有技术背景。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never wrote a single line of code in my life almost.
zh: 我这辈子几乎从未写过一行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've written a couple of console logs manually and that's about it.
zh: 我手动写过几行控制台日志（console logs），仅此而已。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I very much lean onto AI assistance.
zh: 所以我非常依赖 AI 辅助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me actually follow that thread because that's such a good point.
zh: 让我实际上顺着这个线索说下去，因为那是如此好的一个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And something that when we were chatting earlier, you pointed out your feeling is it's actually an advantage to not have a technical background when you get into this space.
zh: 还有一件事，当我们早些时候聊天时，你指出你的感觉是，当你进入这个领域时，没有技术背景实际上是一个优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I honestly feel that it is because people like me don't know that they are not supposed to be building X, Y, Z. And that's how we actually are able to build it.
zh: 我确实感觉是这样，因为像我这样的人不知道他们不应该构建 X、Y、Z。而这实际上就是我们能够构建它的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me give you an example.
zh: 让我举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Six, seven months ago, somebody in our community was like, "Oh, I wish Lovable can build Chrome extensions."
zh: 六七个月前，我们社区里的某个人说，“噢，我希望 Lovable 能构建 Chrome 扩展程序。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then folks that are not technical were like, "Well, why is that not possible?"
zh: 然后非技术人士就说，“嗯，为什么那是不可能的？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then people that are technical start explaining to you, "Oh, well, it's React, it's different stack, it's this."
zh: 然后技术人员开始向你解释，“噢，那是 React，那是不同的堆栈（stack），是这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And people like me, including myself, would just go into Lovable and like, "Build me a Chrome extension based on this app."
zh: 而像我这样的人，包括我自己，就会直接进入 Lovable，说，“基于这个应用给我构建一个 Chrome 扩展程序。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was able to do that with Lovable.
zh: 我能够用 Lovable 做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: There were people that were able to build desktop applications on Lovable.
zh: 有人能够在 Lovable 上构建桌面应用程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, something that shouldn't be possible, it simply is.
zh: 同样，这是一件不应该可能的事情，但它就是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our community manager with me, at one point, she was building this presentation deck for something.
zh: 我们的社区经理和我在一起，有一次，她正在为某件事构建这个演示文稿文稿（deck）。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's like, "Wouldn't it be cool if this was a video?"
zh: 她说，“如果这是一个视频会不会很酷？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she just prompted her way into generating an actual video inside Lovable before that was available.
zh: 然后她只是通过提示（prompted）她的方式在 Lovable 内部生成了一个实际的视频，而在那功能可用之前。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now that's a feature.
zh: 现在这已经是一个功能了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now you can prompt Lovable to do it.
zh: 现在你可以提示（prompt）Lovable 去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But back in the day when she did it, even I thought it was impossible.
zh: 但在她做这件事的当时，连我都认为那是不可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never tried it.
zh: 我从未尝试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's the advantage that we have over people that are technical.
zh: 所以我认为这就是我们相比懂技术的人所拥有的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just coming to this completely unbiased and very positively delusional, which I think you have to have when working with AI tools.
zh: 我们只是带着完全无偏见和非常积极的妄想来到这里，我认为这在处理 AI 工具时是必须具备的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to come with this delusion that absolutely everything is possible until proven wrong.
zh: 你必须带着这种绝对的妄想，认为一切皆有可能，直到被证明是错的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's just the pursuit that I have in my mind that has helped me, among other things that we'll chat today, I think to excel in this role that I have at Lovable.
zh: 这就是我心中一直追求的，它帮助了我，除了我们今天要聊的其他事情之外，我认为它帮助我在 Lovable 扮演的这个角色中脱颖而出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two of the, I think, concerns maybe traps people that don't have a technical background fall into in theory, one is if you get blocked, it's not obvious how to solve a problem.
zh: 我认为非技术背景的人可能掉进的陷阱或顾虑中，有两个，理论上，第一是如果你被卡住了，如何解决问题并不是显而易见的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two is just, are you building this teetering slop that will collapse someday because you don't know system architecture, you don't know if this is going to scale, those sorts of things?
zh: 第二就是，你正在构建的会不会是一种摇摇欲坠的烂摊子，某天会崩塌，因为你不懂系统架构，你不知道这是否能扩展，诸如此类的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: So coming back to what you've learned about how to be successful and build successful products, talk us through just things you've done and things you've learned for how to avoid those sort of things and what you do when you get stuck as one example.
zh: 所以回到你学到的关于如何成功并构建成功产品的经验，带我们过一下你做过的事情和你学到的东西，关于如何避免这类事情，以及当你卡住时你会怎么做，举个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm happy that you mentioned those limitations.
zh: 我很高兴你提到了那些局限性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have some other ones that I want to bring in, but let's address this one first, which is the most important one.
zh: 我还有一些其他想引入的局限性，但让我们先解决这个问题，这是最重要的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that is you have to be self-aware.
zh: 那就是你必须有自我意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I didn't come into this... Yes, I am delusional, as I mentioned, in the sense that I just don't want to accept something's not possible, but I'm also well aware that I need to be better in order for it to become a reality from my own point of view and my own sake.
zh: 我进入这行时并不是……是的，我是有妄想的，正如我所提到的，在这个意义上，我只是不想接受有些事情是不可能的，但我也非常清楚，为了让它从我的角度和为了我自己的利益成为现实，我需要变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I understood very early that coding is not the problem that we're solving for here, that the problem we're solving for is clarity.
zh: 所以我很早就明白，编码不是我们要解决的问题，我们要解决的问题是清晰度。

speaker: Unknown
en: The output that AI can do is much faster than human output anyways.
zh: AI 能够做到的输出无论如何都比人类输出快得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So very early on, I started leveraging chat mode.
zh: 所以很早以前，我就开始利用聊天模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to this day, I can say I spent 80% of my time in planning and chatting and only 20% in executing the plan actually.
zh: 直到今天，我可以说我花了 80% 的时间在规划和聊天上，只有 20% 用于实际执行计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm optimizing for the right kind of speed.
zh: 我正在优化正确的那种速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most people optimize for the wrong one.
zh: 大多数人优化的是错误的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the first lesson that I learned literally on day two, because I came into Lovable, that was my first exposure to this.
zh: 这是我在第二天学到的第一课，因为我加入 Lovable 时，这是我第一次接触这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've tested and played around with all the tools, obviously, but whether somebody's doing it in Cursor or Claude Code, doesn't matter where you are, the problem remains the same.
zh: 显然，我测试和玩过所有的工具，但无论有人是在 Cursor 还是在 Claude Code 上做，都不重要你在哪里，问题依然存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to be clear on what you want to do and you need to know what you're doing because these are still just tools.
zh: 你必须清楚你想做什么，你需要知道你在做什么，因为这些仍然只是工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, AGI is coming, but it's not there yet.
zh: 是的，AGI 正在到来，但它还没到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: So until it's here, you're still steering the ship.
zh: 所以在它到来之前，你仍然在掌舵这艘船。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order for you to steer the ship, you have to know the instructions, right?
zh: 为了掌舵这艘船，你必须知道指令，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And the best way to learn is by building, but treating these tools almost as technical co-founders and educators, and learning while doing, and religiously reading the agent output.
zh: 学习的最佳方式是通过构建，但将这些工具几乎视为技术联合创始人和教育者，在做中学，并虔诚地阅读智能体输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not the code output.
zh: 而不是代码输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't care about the code.
zh: 我不在乎代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: The syntax is none of my interest.
zh: 语法不是我感兴趣的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what the agent tells me that matters to me.
zh: 智能体告诉我的事情才是我关心的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I put a lot of trust in LLMs and AI these days, and I understand that there may be some people that are not as confident as I am.
zh: 这些天我对 LLM 和 AI 寄予了很大的信任，我理解可能有一些人不像我这样自信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I just feel that the models today are good enough for me to trust in their syntax output.
zh: 我只是觉得今天的模型已经足够好了，我可以信任它们的语法输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, I'm concerned about the agent output because of the two limitations that I want to tackle on next.
zh: 然而，我担心智能体的输出，因为我接下来要解决的两个局限性。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one being that there's a limitation when you work with LLMs.
zh: 第一个是当你使用 LLM 时存在局限性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a machine level limitation and there's a human level limitation.
zh: 所以有一个机器层面的局限性和一个人类层面的局限性。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one is there's something that is known as the context memory window.
zh: 第一个是有一个被称为上下文记忆窗口的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for non-technical people, I like to use the Aladdin and the Genie analogy when I explain.
zh: 对于非技术人员，我喜欢用阿拉丁和精灵的类比来解释。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very simple.
zh: 这很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everybody knows the storyline.
zh: 每个人都知道故事情节。

speaker: Unknown
en: You rub the lamp, a genie comes out and tells you, "Okay, I'll grant you three wishes.
zh: 你擦神灯，一个精灵出来告诉你，“好的，我会满足你三个愿望。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not 3,000 wishes, not three million, just three at a time."
zh: 不是 3000 个愿望，不是三百万个，一次只有三个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, when I translate it into working with AI, that simply means, "Hey, I can only make so many requests within a request at a time for AI to be able to listen, understand what it needs to do, scope it, do the research, read, take all the actions, all the inputs and ingredients that it needs to produce a high quality output."
zh: 对我来说，当我把它转化为与 AI 一起工作时，这仅仅意味着，“嘿，我在一个请求中一次只能发出这么多的请求，以便 AI 能够倾听，理解它需要做什么，确定范围，做研究，阅读，采取所有行动，以及生产高质量输出所需的所有输入和要素。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the first part, understanding that there's a limit and it's denominated in tokens.
zh: 所以这是第一部分，明白存在一个限制，并且它是以代币计量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe that's going to be different a year from now, but today there's a token limitation.
zh: 也许一年后会有所不同，但今天存在代币限制。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll take an arbitrary number of 100,000 tokens, for example.
zh: 我会取一个任意的数字 100,000 个代币，例如。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you make a request, a part of those tokens AI spends to read stuff, another to browse the web, another to think, and then another to execute the code.
zh: 所以当你发出请求时，AI 花费一部分代币来阅读东西，一部分来浏览网页，一部分来思考，然后另一部分来执行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then there comes the second limitation, which is you, me and you, humans, which is, let's go back to the analogy of the Genie and the Aladdin.
zh: 然后出现第二个局限性，那就是你，我和你，人类，也就是让我们回到阿拉丁和精灵的类比。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked the Genie for the first wish, and the first wish is I want to be taller.
zh: 我向精灵许了第一个愿望，第一个愿望是我想要长得更高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And guess what happens?
zh: 猜猜发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Genie makes me 13 feet tall.
zh: 精灵让我长到了 13 英尺高。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of a sudden, I can't sit in the car, I can't get into my house.
zh: 突然，我坐不进车里，进不了我的房子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a dysfunctional human being because I was not specific.
zh: 我是一个功能失调的人类，因为我不够具体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the part that we need to optimize for today, it's going to get better, but today it's still not there yet, is that AI just don't understand what do you mean when you say, "You know what I mean?"
zh: 所以我们今天需要优化的部分，它以后会变好，但今天它还达不到那个水平，就是 AI 就是不知道你是什么意思，当你说，“你知道我的意思？”时。

speaker: Unknown
en: You do when I tell you that.
zh: 你知道当我告诉你那个的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: We as humans, I'm 36, so I have 36 years of experience of living as a human to know what you mean, but AI doesn't have that.
zh: 我们作为人类，我 36 岁，所以我拥有 36 年作为人类生活的经验来知道你是什么意思，但 AI 没有那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need to be specific, you need to provide references, you need to provide the right context.
zh: 所以你需要具体，你需要提供参考，你需要提供正确的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I've learned is how to combat that part.
zh: 所以我学到的是如何对抗那部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think because I can't control the first part, which is the token memory window, the quality of the LLM models, you are 100% control of the latter.
zh: 而且我认为因为我无法控制第一部分，也就是 token 记忆窗口，LLM 模型的质量，你是 100% 控制后者的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what I want to dive into today as well and just try to teach people, "Okay, if I'm the malleable part, how do I fix that part?"
zh: 这也是我想今天深入探讨的内容，并尝试教导人们，“好吧，如果我是可塑的部分，我如何修正那部分？”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the key lesson here.
zh: 我认为这是这里的关键课程。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is so helpful.
zh: 这太有帮助了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I love this metaphor of the Genie.
zh: 而且我喜欢精灵的这个隐喻。

speaker: Unknown
en: This piece about clarity is such a thread I've been noticing across people that have been successful using AI tools.
zh: 关于清晰度的这一点是我在那些成功使用 AI 工具的人身上注意到的一个共同线索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like an emerging core skill is learning clarity in the ask of the AI.
zh: 感觉像是一个正在涌现的核心技能是学习在向 AI 提问时的清晰度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have any advice or anything you do there to help be better at being clear with what you want?
zh: 你有什么建议或者你做什么来帮助你在这方面变得更清楚你想要什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first of all, as you said yourself right now, you need to be good at understanding what clarity means and how to translate it.
zh: 所以首先，正如你现在自己所说的，你需要擅长理解清晰度意味着什么以及如何翻译它。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my terms, clarity means understanding what tasteful looks like, what's good enough versus what's world-class, what's magical.
zh: 在我的术语中，清晰度意味着理解什么是有品位的，什么是足够好的 vs 什么是世界级的，什么是神奇的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I developed that through something that I heard from you, you mentioned before, which is exposure time, making sure that I'm exposing myself to content and to people and to relationships or whatever that are going to help me to level up in that domain.
zh: 我是通过我听你说过的一件事发展出那点的，你之前提到过的，那就是曝光时间，确保我让自己接触内容、人和关系或任何能帮助我在那个领域提升的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, it goes back to self-awareness.
zh: 同样，这又回到了自我意识。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew even before I joined Lovable, I was like, "Okay."
zh: 我甚至在加入 Lovable 之前就知道，我当时就想，“好的。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Even before I started using Lovable or any AI tools, first thing that I knew was like, "I don't know how to code."
zh: 甚至在我开始使用 Lovable 或任何 AI 工具之前，我第一件知道的事就是，“我不知道怎么写代码。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So my first thing was like, "Oh, I can build.
zh: 所以我的第一件事就是，“噢，我可以构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, amazing."
zh: 哇，真了不起。”

speaker: Unknown
en: But a week later it was like, "Oh, I can build, but I'm not fast enough."
zh: 但一周后就是，“噢，我可以构建，但我不够快。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So I optimized for speed.
zh: 所以我为速度做了优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was like, "Oh, I can build and I can build so fast."
zh: 所以我想，“噢，我可以构建，而且我可以构建得非常快。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then two weeks later, my development cycle that I'm in began, and it's still ongoing, which is, "Wait a minute, should I have even built this in the first place?"
zh: 然后两周后，我进入了我的开发周期，而且它还在持续，那就是，“等一下，我一开始到底该不该构建这个？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Because once you figure out that we solved for the how, which is AI assistant or rapid engineering, call it whatever you want, you can call it vibe coding if you want to, but we solve for that.
zh: 因为一旦你发现我们解决了 how 的问题，也就是 AI 助手或 rapid engineering，随你怎么称呼，如果你想叫它 vibe coding 也可以，但我们解决了那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we got to solve for everything else.
zh: 现在我们得解决其他所有事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everything else is what matters.
zh: 而其他所有事才是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Good design, good taste, good user experience.
zh: 好的设计，好的品位，好的用户体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you think about who you're building stuff for with these tools, you're building it for humans.
zh: 当你考虑你在为谁用这些工具构建东西时，你是为人类构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans are emotional beings and we all make our purchasing or any kind of decisions on an emotional basis.
zh: 人类是情感生物，我们都在情感基础上做出我们的购买或任何类型的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that the core skill there to work on and develop today isn't, again, coding, although I have nothing against traditional engineering.
zh: 所以我认为今天在那里工作和发展的核心技能不是，再次强调，写代码，虽然我不反对传统工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll say later why.
zh: 我稍后会解释原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm actually a big fan of it, of elite engineering, but people like me, people watching that are like, "Should I start learning how to code?"
zh: 实际上我是它的超级粉丝，精英工程，但是像我这样的人，观看的人就像是，“我应该开始学习怎么写代码吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: If you haven't done it yet, I'd honestly say no.
zh: 如果你还没做那个，我会诚实地说不。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're optimizing for the wrong skillset.
zh: 你在为错误的技能集做优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't be rewarded in the world of AI for faster raw output; we will be rewarded for better judgment.
zh: 我们不会在 AI 世界中因为更快的原始产出而获得回报；我们会因为更好的判断力而获得回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that better judgment comes with, again, to go back to your question, how are you solving for that?
zh: 所以我认为更好的判断力伴随着，再次回到你的问题，你在如何解决那个？

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you solving for this?
zh: 你在如何解决这个？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it starts with exposure.
zh: 嗯，它始于曝光。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm deliberately exposing myself to people and resources that I know I need to consume to level up.
